proposal_record.raw:
{
  "diagnosis": "Recurring failures share three causes: (1) a stated medicine or patient fact is not carried forward into the final choice, so interaction/contraindication or comorbidity constraints are missed; (2) when multiple options are same-class or indication-appropriate, the agent defaults to the first listed or alphabetically early option instead of using the dialogue-specific fact that discriminates them; (3) the agent over-infers contraindications from family history or incidental medicines, or invents a safety concern not stated, then avoids the correct drug.",
  "skills": [
    {
      "id": "extract_meds_and_conditions",
      "text": "Before selecting, list every currently taken medicine and every stated active condition/comorbidity exactly as named in the dialogue. Treat each as a hard constraint in the safety check, not background. A stated drug that can interact with or be contraindicated by a candidate must influence selection."
    },
    {
      "id": "indication_first_then_safety",
      "text": "Select candidates only from options that treat the stated diagnosis. Eliminate options whose labeled indication does not match. Only among indication-appropriate options apply patient-specific safety and interaction constraints."
    },
    {
      "id": "choose_the_discriminating_fact",
      "text": "When two or more options are in the same class or both plausibly treat the diagnosis, do not default to order of appearance. Identify the one dialogue fact that distinguishes them (a stated interacting medicine, a comorbidity, a symptom severity, a pregnancy, a renal/hepatic issue) and use it to break the tie."
    },
    {
      "id": "named_interaction_lookup",
      "text": "If a currently taken medicine is named, check each candidate for a known clinically significant interaction with it before choosing. If one candidate is specifically flagged as interacting and another equally effective option lacks the interaction, prefer the non-interacting one."
    },
    {
      "id": "no_invented_contraindications",
      "text": "Do not treat family history, a relative's condition, or an unrelated medicine as a contraindication for the patient unless the dialogue states the patient personally has that condition or a documented reaction. Absence of a stated contraindication means no contraindication."
    },
    {
      "id": "avoid_incidental_wording",
      "text": "Do not avoid an indicated drug because the doctor mentions caution, monitoring, or 'we may need to adjust.' Stated caution is not a contraindication. Choose the drug indicated for the diagnosis unless a real stated patient-specific barrier exists."
    },
    {
      "id": "class_preference_by_severity",
      "text": "For inflammatory, allergic, or immune conditions, distinguish acute/severe presentations from mild/localized ones: systemic corticosteroids are preferred for acute systemic inflammation, while topical or narrow-spectrum agents are preferred for localized skin conditions. Match the option's route/spectrum to the stated severity and distribution."
    },
    {
      "id": "report_evidence_span",
      "text": "Before finalizing, state the exact phrase(s) from the dialogue that establish the diagnosis, the current medicine(s), and any patient-specific safety fact used. If a constraint was assumed rather than quoted, discard it."
    }
  ],
  "focus_terms": [
    "I'm currently taking",
    "I take",
    "I've been taking",
    "for my",
    "my medical history",
    "family history",
    "I'm allergic",
    "contraindicated",
    "interaction",
    "diagnosis is",
    "you may have",
    "likely related to",
    "heavy menstrual bleeding",
    "uterine fibroids",
    "bipolar disorder",
    "mania",
    "depression with anxiety",
    "perioral dermatitis",
    "Salmonella",
    "gastroenteritis",
    "hyperlipoproteinemia",
    "chylomicrons",
    "VLDL",
    "lupus",
    "nephritis",
    "photosensitivity",
    "malar rash",
    "foamy urine",
    "inflammatory condition",
    "allergic reaction"
  ],
  "modules": {
    "patient_evidence": "Extract and list the stated primary diagnosis, every current medicine, and every personally stated comorbidity or symptom. Quote exact dialogue phrases for each. Flag which extracted facts are patient-specific versus family history or incidental. Do not record a fact that was not stated.",
    "safety_check": "For each indication-appropriate candidate, check it against the current medicines list for known interactions and against personal comorbidities for contraindications. Use only patient-specific stated facts. Do not infer a contraindication from family history or from a doctor's general caution. If no interaction or contraindication is stated between a candidate and a stated medicine/condition, do not invent one.",
    "option_selection": "First restrict to options indicated for the stated diagnosis. If several remain, apply interaction/contraindication results to remove unsafe options, then use the single dialogue fact that discriminates among the survivors. Do not default to first-listed or alphabetical order. If tied and no stated barrier exists, choose the most specifically indicated agent for the stated severity."
  }
}
